title: DyREM: Dynamically Mitigating Quantum Readout Error with Embedded Accelerator
problem: Quantum readout error mitigation requires on-the-fly computation of large mitigation matrices, incurring high latency and memory overhead that limits practical quantum computing scale.
motivation: Quantum systems suffer from measurement errors; efficient mitigation is essential for near-term quantum computing viability.
method: Quantum computers introduce errors during readout measurements. DyREM improves this by exploiting sparsity—the fact that quantum probability distributions contain many zero or near-zero values. Rather than processing large error-correction matrices, DyREM dynamically creates smaller versions. An embedded hardware accelerator performs the required calculations (tensor products), using gating—conditional logic gates—to skip computing certain quantum state values, reducing latency and memory overhead.
key_novelty: DyREM's core idea is that quantum probability distributions are sparse (full of zeros), enabling dynamic shrinking of error-correction matrices through gated computation that skips unnecessary calculations.
contributions: Embedded accelerator architecture with computational gating
limitations: Evaluation limited to specific quantum systems; applicability to other error mitigation schemes and quantum architectures unclear.
